results.title: Elon Musk says millions in Social Security database are between ages of 100 and 159
results.snippet: His post features a chart indicating there are more than 20 million listed with ages 100 and higher, including more than 3.9 million in the 130-139 age range, more than 3.5 million in the 140-149 range and more than 1.3 million in the 150-159 range.

results.title: Elon Musk misreads Social Security data, millions of dead people not getting benefits, experts say | abc7news.com
results.snippet: It started in the Oval Office last week when Musk -- facing reporters for the first time since the Department of Government Efficiency began its aggressive overhaul of the federal government -- said he found "crazy things" in the Social Security system, including, he said, people who are "150 years old."

results.title: SSA marked millions aged 120+ 'deceased' to clean up records. This may help prevent fraud
results.snippet: Audits in 2015 and 2023 found millions of people over 100 years old in the SSA's database without death information, with a small percentage receiving social security payments, leading to concerns about fraud and improper payments.

results.title: Millions Of Active Social Security Numbers Belong To People Over 112 Years Old
results.snippet: As of 2015, about 6.5 million social security numbers registered to people who would have been at least 112 years old had no death date recorded in the SSA’s database, known as Numident.
